title: Hidden Key Cabinet: DIY Build, Buying Guide & Ideas
h1: Hidden Key Cabinet: How to Build, Buy and Place One in Your Kitchen or Entry
description: Build or buy a hidden key cabinet that looks like art: a full DIY cut list and steps, cabinet types compared, placement heights and renter-safe key storage.
excerpt: Give your keys a home that looks like art. Build a picture-frame key cabinet in an afternoon, or choose the right ready-made type for your kitchen or entry.
image_alt: Hidden key cabinet mounted on a kitchen wall with a picture-frame door open to show key hooks inside
key_takeaways: Hang the cabinet where your keys already land, usually within a step or two of the door.
Center it 57 to 60 inches from the floor so it reads as art rather than storage.
Look for at least 1.5 to 2 inches of interior depth so car fobs fit with the door closed.
A DIY picture-frame cabinet takes an afternoon and roughly $40 to $90 in materials.
Label each hook and keep rarely used spares on a separate row.

faq.q: Where is the best place to hang a key cabinet?
faq.a: Hang it on a wall you pass every time you come home, within a few steps of the front door. In many apartments that is the kitchen wall nearest the entry. Center it about 57 to 60 inches from the floor, keep it away from the stove, and avoid lining it up with a street-facing window.

faq.q: How deep should a key cabinet be?
faq.a: Aim for at least 1.5 to 2 inches of interior depth. That leaves room for bulky car fobs and large key rings without the door bulging open. If you want a small shelf for sunglasses or a pen, build or buy one closer to 2.5 inches deep.

faq.q: How do you hide keys in an apartment without drilling?
faq.a: Mount a hook strip inside a cabinet or pantry door with removable adhesive hooks, use a lidded box on a console, or dedicate a drawer with a divided tray. Avoid hanging a loaded key cabinet on adhesive strips alone, since the weight and repeated door opening can pull it off the wall.

faq.q: How much does it cost to make a DIY key cabinet?
faq.a: A simple picture-frame key cabinet typically costs about $40 to $90 in materials, including a wood frame, a pine or poplar board, a plywood back, hinges, a magnetic catch, hooks and a French cleat. Costs rise if you buy a larger custom frame or need to buy tools.

faq.q: Is it safe to keep car keys near the front door?
faq.a: Keeping keys out of sight is sensible. For keyless entry fobs, some thefts involve relaying the fob's signal from inside the home, so consider storing the fob farther from the door or in a signal-blocking pouch. Check your car maker's guidance for your model.
